opening.text: There was a time when doctors came to the house. They carried a black bag. They sat by the bed. They did not mind if it was late at night. If you were sick, they came to you.

The Savior is like that. He does not wait for us to be well enough to come to Him. He goes where we are. He sits with us in the dark hours. He knows the way to every sickroom, every broken heart, and every sleepless night.
Today I want to talk about Jesus Christ as our Healer.

mainMessage.text: During His life, Jesus healed the sick, the blind, the lame, and the lonely. He still heals today. He heals bodies, and He heals hearts. He heals the guilt we carry and the grief we cannot name. He does not always heal in the way or the time we expect. But He never turns away from the one who reaches for Him. And He never stops loving the one who is hurting.

blocks.text: He healed all who came.

The Gospels do not tell of a few healings. They tell of crowds. Wherever Jesus went, people brought their sick. No one was turned away. He healed “all manner of sickness.” And Matthew says that this was the fulfillment of a prophecy about the Savior.

And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. And his fame went throughout all Syria: and they brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatic, and those that had the palsy; and he healed them.

When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits with his word, and healed all that were sick: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.
Elder C. Scott Grow of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Miracle of the Atonement” from the April 2011 general conference.

Jesus Christ is the Great Healer of our souls. . . . When we sin, Satan tells us we are lost. In contrast, our Redeemer offers redemption to all—no matter what we have done wrong—even to you and to me.
“Even to you and to me.” That is the part to hold on to.
He heals those who reach for Him.

One woman had been sick for twelve years. She had gone to many doctors. She had spent everything. Nothing worked. So she did a brave and quiet thing. She reached out and touched the edge of His clothes.

And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse, When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. . . . And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
Elder Donald L. Hallstrom of the Seventy gave this counsel in his talk “Turn to the Lord” from the April 2010 general conference.

. . . And, without delay, turn to the Lord. Exercise all of the faith you have in Him. Let Him share your burden. Allow His grace to lighten your load. . . . Never let an earthly circumstance disable you spiritually.
She did not wait until she felt strong enough. She reached out in the middle of her weakness. So can we.
He heals broken hearts.

Some wounds cannot be seen. A heart can be broken by loss, by betrayal, by years of loneliness. Isaiah wrote of One who would come to bind up the brokenhearted. Jesus read those words in the synagogue and said they were about Him.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,
He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Atonement Covers All Pain” from the April 2011 general conference.

All that will come may be ‘clasped in the arms of Jesus.’ All souls can be healed by His power. All pain can be soothed. In Him, we can ‘find rest unto \[our\] souls.’ Our mortal circumstances may not immediately change, but our pain, worry, suffering, and fear can be swallowed up in His peace and healing balm.
Notice how honest that is. Our circumstances may not change at once. But our pain can still be soothed.
He heals the weight of sin.

There is a kind of sickness we do not talk about. Guilt. It makes us feel heavy and ashamed. The Savior knows that weight. He invites us to bring it to Him. In the Book of Mormon, He told the Nephites He wanted to heal them. And in the Gospel of Matthew, He called the weary to come and rest.
O all ye that are spared because ye were more righteous than they, will ye not now return unto me, and repent of your sins, and be converted, that I may heal you?

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repent . . . That I May Heal You” from the October 2009 general conference.

I testify that the Savior is able and eager to forgive our sins. Except for the sins of those few who choose perdition after having known a fulness, there is no sin that cannot be forgiven. What a marvelous privilege for each of us to turn away from our sins and to come unto Christ. Divine forgiveness is one of the sweetest fruits of the gospel, removing guilt and pain from our hearts and replacing them with joy and peace of conscience.
“Able and eager.” He is not reluctant. He is waiting.
He heals in His own way and time.

Some of us have prayed for healing and have not seen it yet. That is a hard place to be. The scriptures give us a promise. Nephi saw that the Savior would rise “with healing in his wings.” And John saw a day when every tear would be wiped away.

Behold, they will crucify him; and after he is laid in a sepulchre for the space of three days he shall rise from the dead, with healing in his wings; and all those who shall believe on his name shall be saved in the kingdom of God. Wherefore, my soul delighteth to prophesy concerning him, for I have seen his day, and my heart doth magnify his holy name.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ—the Master Healer” from the October 2005 general conference.

I know that feeling! I know the fears and tears of such moments. But I also know that our prayers are never ignored. Our faith is never unappreciated. I know that an all-wise Heavenly Father’s perspective is much broader than is ours. While we know of our mortal problems and pain, He knows of our immortal progress and potential. If we pray to know His will and submit ourselves to it with patience and courage, heavenly healing can take place in His own way and time.
His way and His time. That does not mean He is absent. It means He sees more than we do.
He is still healing today.
The Savior did not stop healing when He left Galilee. When He visited the Nephites, He asked a simple question. Do you have anyone who is sick? Bring them here. And He healed every one.

Have ye any that are sick among you? Bring them hither. Have ye any that are lame, or blind, or halt, or maimed, or leprous, or that are withered, or that are deaf, or that are afflicted in any manner? Bring them hither and I will heal them, for I have compassion upon you; my bowels are filled with mercy. For I perceive that ye desire that I should show unto you what I have done unto your brethren at Jerusalem, for I see that your faith is sufficient that I should heal you. And it came to pass that when he had thus spoken, all the multitude, with one accord, did go forth with their sick and their afflicted, and their lame, and with their blind, and with their dumb, and with all them that were afflicted in any manner; and he did heal them every one as they were brought forth unto him.
President Russell M. Nelson said this in his talk “We Can Do Better and Be Better” from the April 2019 general conference.

Too many people consider repentance as punishment—something to be avoided. . . . But this feeling of being penalized is engendered by Satan. He tries to block us from looking to Jesus Christ, who stands with open arms, hoping and willing to heal, forgive, cleanse, strengthen, purify, and sanctify us.
Open arms. That is how He stands. He is still waiting for us to bring Him what hurts.

story.title: The man let down through the roof

blocks.text: Four friends carried a man who could not walk. The house where Jesus was teaching was full. They could not get in. So they climbed up and opened the roof. Then they lowered their friend down to the Lord.

And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four. And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay. When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.
I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house. And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.
Notice that the Lord saw their faith, not only the man’s. Sometimes we cannot get to the Savior on our own. We need friends who will carry us. And sometimes we are the ones who carry.

application.text: First, name one thing in your life that needs healing. It may be a body, a heart, or a relationship. Take it to the Lord in prayer this week. Be specific. Second, ask yourself whom you can carry to Him. A friend, a family member, a neighbor. Offer to pray with them or sit with them. Third, if guilt is the weight you carry, talk to your bishop. He can help you take the next step toward healing.

story.title: The ten lepers

blocks.text: Ten men with leprosy stood far off and called to Jesus. They were outcasts. They had to live apart from everyone. Jesus told them to go and show themselves to the priests. As they went, they were healed. Only one came back.

And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us. And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed. And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
Ten were healed, and one came back. The one heard something more: “thy faith hath made thee whole.” Gratitude opens a deeper kind of healing.

application.text: First, if you are waiting for healing, ask the Lord what He wants you to do while you wait. Listen for even a small answer. Second, say thank you. Name three ways the Lord has already helped you this month. Third, visit someone who is in a cast of their own, whether sick, grieving, or alone. Sit with them. You do not need to fix anything.

God built healing into the world. It is part of how things work. And the Savior carries that same gift into our deepest needs.
I would like to talk about Jesus Christ as the Healer.

story.title: The man at the pool of Bethesda

blocks.text: Beside the pool of Bethesda lay a crowd of people who were sick, blind, or lame. One man had been there thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him, He asked a surprising question.

And a certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years. When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he saith unto him, Wilt thou be made whole? The impotent man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me. Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy bed, and walk. And immediately the man was made whole, and took up his bed, and walked: and on the same day was the sabbath.
Thirty-eight years. The Savior noticed him. He asked, “Wilt thou be made whole?” He does not force healing on anyone. He asks. And when the man said yes, in his own way, the Lord healed him.

application.text: First, ask yourself the Savior’s question. “Wilt thou be made whole?” Answer it honestly in prayer. Second, be patient with your own healing and with the healing of others. Do not rush a person who is grieving. Third, share one thing that has helped you heal with someone who needs it. It may be a hymn, a scripture, or a kind word.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that Jesus Christ heals. I know that He healed in Galilee, and that He heals now. I know that He has never given up on me. I know that when I turn to Him, I find rest. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to answer the Savior's question, "Wilt thou be made whole?" honestly in prayer.
I invite you to be patient with your own healing and with others.

closingVerse.text: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.

opening.text: Think of a nurse who works the night shift. Everyone else is asleep. The halls are quiet. A patient presses the call button at two in the morning, afraid, in pain. The nurse comes. She sits down. She says, “I’m here.”
That small act can mean everything. It is not a cure. But it is care.
The Savior is the Healer who stays through the night. He is there when no one else is awake. I would like to talk about that today.

mainMessage.text: Jesus Christ healed bodies, hearts, and souls. He healed those who came to Him, and those who were brought by friends. He still heals today. His healing may not always look like what we hope for, but it is always real. He stays with us in the long nights, and He does not leave until the work is done. All He asks is that we call.

blocks.text: He was never too busy to heal.

Imagine the schedule of the Lord in Galilee. Crowds pressed in on Him every day. People came at all hours. And He healed them, one at a time. He did not tire of them. The prophet Isaiah had said He would take our sicknesses upon Him.

And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. And his fame went throughout all Syria: and they brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatic, and those that had the palsy; and he healed them.

When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits with his word, and healed all that were sick: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.
Elder C. Scott Grow of the Seventy taught this in his talk “The Miracle of the Atonement” from the April 2011 general conference.

Jesus Christ is the Great Healer of our souls. . . . When we sin, Satan tells us we are lost. In contrast, our Redeemer offers redemption to all—no matter what we have done wrong—even to you and to me.
The verse says, “when the even was come.” They came in the evening. The day was over. And still He healed.
He answers the one who calls.

The woman with the issue of blood did not call out. She just reached. But the principle is the same. When we turn toward Him, He turns toward us. The Lord stopped everything to find her and speak to her.

And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse, When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. . . . And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
Elder Donald L. Hallstrom of the Seventy gave this invitation in his talk “Turn to the Lord” from the April 2010 general conference.

. . . And, without delay, turn to the Lord. Exercise all of the faith you have in Him. Let Him share your burden. Allow His grace to lighten your load. . . . Never let an earthly circumstance disable you spiritually.
Press the call button. He will come.
He tends the heart.

Some of the deepest pain happens in the heart. A lost friendship. A child who has gone away. A dream that did not come true. The Lord knows. He came to heal the brokenhearted, and He binds up their wounds.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,
He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Atonement Covers All Pain” from the April 2011 general conference.

All that will come may be ‘clasped in the arms of Jesus.’ All souls can be healed by His power. All pain can be soothed. In Him, we can ‘find rest unto \[our\] souls.’ Our mortal circumstances may not immediately change, but our pain, worry, suffering, and fear can be swallowed up in His peace and healing balm.
A nurse may not cure the illness. But she sits with the patient, and that helps. The Savior does both.
He heals the soul.

There is a kind of night we make for ourselves. We make mistakes. We feel ashamed. We avoid the light. The Lord does not leave us in that night. He invites us back. He wants to heal us and give us rest.
O all ye that are spared because ye were more righteous than they, will ye not now return unto me, and repent of your sins, and be converted, that I may heal you?

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles testified of this in his talk “Repent . . . That I May Heal You” from the October 2009 general conference.

I testify that the Savior is able and eager to forgive our sins. Except for the sins of those few who choose perdition after having known a fulness, there is no sin that cannot be forgiven. What a marvelous privilege for each of us to turn away from our sins and to come unto Christ. Divine forgiveness is one of the sweetest fruits of the gospel, removing guilt and pain from our hearts and replacing them with joy and peace of conscience.
Peace of conscience. That is the morning after a hard night.
He stays until morning.

Some of us are in the middle of a long night right now. We have prayed and waited. Nothing has changed. The scriptures say the Lord will come with healing. He rises, and there is healing in His wings. And in the end, He wipes away every tear.

Behold, they will crucify him; and after he is laid in a sepulchre for the space of three days he shall rise from the dead, with healing in his wings; and all those who shall believe on his name shall be saved in the kingdom of God. Wherefore, my soul delighteth to prophesy concerning him, for I have seen his day, and my heart doth magnify his holy name.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ—the Master Healer” from the October 2005 general conference.

I know that feeling! I know the fears and tears of such moments. But I also know that our prayers are never ignored. Our faith is never unappreciated. I know that an all-wise Heavenly Father’s perspective is much broader than is ours. While we know of our mortal problems and pain, He knows of our immortal progress and potential. If we pray to know His will and submit ourselves to it with patience and courage, heavenly healing can take place in His own way and time.
Our prayers are never ignored. He is on the night shift, and He is still with us.
He is here now.
The Lord asked the Nephites to bring those who were sick. He is still asking us today. If you know someone who is hurting, bring them to Him. If it is you, come yourself.

Have ye any that are sick among you? Bring them hither. Have ye any that are lame, or blind, or halt, or maimed, or leprous, or that are withered, or that are deaf, or that are afflicted in any manner? Bring them hither and I will heal them, for I have compassion upon you; my bowels are filled with mercy. For I perceive that ye desire that I should show unto you what I have done unto your brethren at Jerusalem, for I see that your faith is sufficient that I should heal you. And it came to pass that when he had thus spoken, all the multitude, with one accord, did go forth with their sick and their afflicted, and their lame, and with their blind, and with their dumb, and with all them that were afflicted in any manner; and he did heal them every one as they were brought forth unto him.
President Russell M. Nelson taught this in his talk “We Can Do Better and Be Better” from the April 2019 general conference.

Too many people consider repentance as punishment—something to be avoided. . . . But this feeling of being penalized is engendered by Satan. He tries to block us from looking to Jesus Christ, who stands with open arms, hoping and willing to heal, forgive, cleanse, strengthen, purify, and sanctify us.
He is not far. He is the nearest one.

story.title: Blind Bartimaeus

blocks.text: Bartimaeus sat by the road outside Jericho, begging. When he heard that Jesus was passing, he cried out for mercy. People told him to be quiet. He cried out louder.

And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimæus, the son of Timæus, sat by the highway side begging. And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me. And many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me. And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee. And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus. And Jesus answered and said unto him, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight. And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.
The crowd told him to be quiet. The Lord stopped. He called him. He asked what he wanted. Then He healed him. When others tell us to be quiet about our pain, the Savior still stops to listen.

application.text: First, tonight, tell the Lord something you have been holding in. Do not worry about how it sounds. Second, be a night-shift friend to someone this week. A text, a call, a visit. Say, “I’m here.” Third, when you feel afraid, remember Bartimaeus. Cry out. The Lord will stop.

opening.text: Picture a sickroom at night. The curtains are drawn. The air is heavy. Then someone lights a candle. It does not fill the room with sunlight. But the dark is no longer complete. The sick person can see the face of a loved one, and that changes everything.
The Savior is that light in our hardest rooms. He does not always take the night away at once. But He is there, and we are not alone.
I would like to talk about Jesus Christ as the Healer.

mainMessage.text: The Savior healed many people in the Holy Land, and He heals people today. He heals bodies, broken hearts, and troubled souls. Sometimes the healing is quick. Often it comes slowly, in His time. But it is real. He invites us to come to Him, and He never turns anyone away.

blocks.text: He healed every person who came.

The scriptures do not say He healed a few. They say He healed all manner of sickness. When evening came, people brought their sick to Him, and no one went home untouched. Matthew says this fulfilled what Isaiah had said. The Messiah would carry our sicknesses.

And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. No one is too far gone. That includes you and me.
He responds to faith, even a trembling kind.
The woman who touched His garment was afraid. She did not ask for attention. She only hoped. And that was enough. He turned, He saw her, and He called her daughter.

And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
Elder Donald L. Hallstrom of the Seventy gave this counsel in his talk “Turn to the Lord” from the April 2010 general conference.

. . . And, without delay, turn to the Lord. Exercise all of the faith you have in Him. Let Him share your burden. Allow His grace to lighten your load. . . . Never let an earthly circumstance disable you spiritually.
Light one candle of faith. He will meet you there.
He comforts the brokenhearted.
Some hurts do not show on a chart. A death in the family. A broken promise. A long season of loneliness. The Savior came for these too. He came to heal the brokenhearted and to bind up wounds.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,

The room may stay the same. But we are no longer alone in it.
He lifts the weight of sin.
Guilt is heavy. It makes the room feel small and dark. But the Lord calls us out of it. He asks us to return, and promises to heal us. He also offers a lighter yoke.
O all ye that are spared because ye were more righteous than they, will ye not now return unto me, and repent of your sins, and be converted, that I may heal you?

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

Divine forgiveness is one of the sweetest fruits of the gospel, removing guilt and pain from our hearts and replacing them with joy and peace of conscience.
Eager. He is not reluctant. He is eager.
He heals in His own time.
A candle burns slowly. It does not rush the dawn. But it keeps burning until morning comes. The scriptures promise that healing is in His wings, and that He will one day wipe away every tear.

His own way and time. We can trust that.
He is still healing.
When the Savior visited the Nephites, He did not just teach. He healed. He asked for the sick to be brought to Him, and He healed every one. That invitation has not expired.

Have ye any that are lame, or blind, or halt, or maimed, or leprous, or that are withered, or that are deaf, or that are afflicted in any manner? Open arms. That is how He waits for us.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time about the Savior as Healer. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus heals Malchus

blocks.text: This happened on the night of His arrest. The Savior was about to be taken away. He was about to suffer and die. And yet, in the middle of that terrible hour, He stopped to heal an enemy.
And one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear. And Jesus answered and said, Suffer ye thus far. And he touched his ear, and healed him.

The man was part of the crowd that came to arrest Him. John tells us his name was Malchus. The Lord had every reason to think only of Himself. Instead, He reached out and healed. His mercy reaches even those who are against Him.

application.text: First, name one hurt you have been carrying, and take it to the Lord in prayer this week. Second, be a light for someone in a dark room. Visit them, call them, or sit with them. Third, think of someone who has wronged you. Ask the Lord to help you wish them well, as He healed the one who came to arrest Him.
